summary.text: A male neonate born by elective caesarian section at 39 weeks to a mother with moderate fetal ascites and polyhydramnios on antenatal ultrasound developed a distended abdomen and respiratory distress 4 hours after birth and was given intranasal oxygen and intravenous fluids.

Packed cell volume fell from 40% to 23%; ultrasound showed hepatosplenomegaly with moderate ascites, the radiograph showed a displaced stomach with ground-glass opacity, and paracentesis showed free flowing non-clotted blood. Malrotation with midgut volvulus was the initial diagnosis.

After transfusion and resuscitation, laparotomy at the 36th hour of life found a 3cm sub capsular splenic laceration and 100 mls of haemoperitoneum with clots, treated with a haemostatic agent (Surgicel) and further whole blood. The final diagnosis was Grade II splenic injury. Six hours post-surgery he had a cardiopulmonary arrest and resuscitation was unsuccessful. Mechanical ventilation was unavailable, so he was ventilated manually; the discussion reports his eventual death.
